headline: Revenue and segment profit grow, net income falls on taxes
summary_short: Disney's fiscal Q2 2026 revenue rose 6.6% y/y to $25,168M and segment operating income rose 3.8% y/y to $4,603M, but net income attributable to Disney fell 31.4% y/y to $2,247M and diluted EPS fell to $1.27 from $1.81, mainly because the prior-year quarter included a one-time tax benefit that did not recur.
summary_long: Revenue growth was driven by higher subscription and affiliate fees, growth at parks and experiences, more content sales, and about 2 points of lift from the Fubo and NFL transactions. Segment operating income rose 3.8% y/y as Entertainment and Experiences growth outweighed a Sports decline from higher programming/production costs. Net income and EPS fell y/y solely because the prior-year quarter booked a tax benefit from resolving a tax matter; income before taxes was up 9.1% y/y. Cash was $5,682M and total equity $115,312M as of March 28, 2026. Disney guided FY2026 content spend (incl. sports rights) to ~$24B (from $23B) and FY2026 capex to ~$9B (from $8B).

drivers.explanation: Higher subscription and affiliate fees, growth at parks and experiences, and increased content sales; the Fubo and NFL transactions added about 2 percentage points of growth.
Entertainment segment operating income rose on higher subscription/affiliate fees; Experiences rose on domestic park and resort growth; Sports fell on higher programming and production costs.
Decline was due to a tax benefit from resolving a tax matter recognized in the prior-year quarter that did not recur; the release states this explicitly as the cause.
Same cause as net income: the prior-year quarter's non-recurring tax benefit, not an operating deterioration (pretax income was up 9.1% y/y).
Company guided FY2026 produced/licensed content spend (incl. sports rights) to ~$24B (from $23B in FY2025) and FY2026 capex to ~$9B (from $8B).
